ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Unified Analysis of Positional Encodings with Application to RoPE
PROPOSAL: Perform a theoretical analysis of the interplay between additive and multiplicative mechanisms for positional encoding, aiming to derive a framework that can encompass all forms of relative and absolute encodings, including but not limited to RoPE, ALiBi, and FoX.
CONTROLS: Compare the derived framework with standalone RoPE, ALiBi, and FoX formulations.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The unified framework is expected to exhibit strong invariance and expressivity properties, with moderate computational overhead when approximating rotation with learned parameters. The RoPE baseline may face difficulties in capturing cross-subspace coupling due to its rigid coordinate planes and log-uniform spectra.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Orthogonal Rotation Network (ORN) - A Learned Framework for Positional Encoding
PROPOSAL: Develop a learned orthogonal rotation network (ORN) that adaptively generates rotational matrices for each position, subsuming both RoPE and additive/multiplicative biases. The network takes in a learnable offset and token embeddings, combining the former to yield a dense, skew-symmetric generator for contextual rotations. The resultant rotation matrices are applied to keys and queries, fostering expressivity and invariance.
CONTROLS: Compare ORN with standalone RoPE and ALiBi, as well as with a naive baseline (i.e. using a fixed rotation matrix for all positions).
COST: 150 GPU-hours (training the ORN and the corresponding models)
PREDICTION: ORN is expected to outperform RoPE by providing adaptive rotations for each position, and approach additive/multiplicative biases in terms of expressivity while having better invariance properties. Challenges may arise from the computational overhead and the choice of learnable offsets.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Orthogonal Rotation Network (ORN) - A Learned Framework for Positional Encoding (Revised)
PROPOSAL: Refine the original ORN proposal to incorporate a key constraint: make sure that the resulting rotation matrices preserve the norms of input query/key embeddings. This constraint is essential for stability and orthogonal invariance. To achieve this, we modify the network's architecture to incorporate a soft constraint-based loss during training, ensuring the rotation matrices have an approximately isometric property.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the revised ORN against the standalone RoPE and ALiBi, as well as the original ORN without norm-preserving constraint.
COST: 100 GPU-hours (fine-tuning the original network to incorporate the norm-preserving constraint)
PREDICTION: The revised ORN is expected to outperform its original version in terms of stability and invariance, as well as its standalone competitors, at a minimal computational cost.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Efficient Implementation of ORN with Split-Depth Architecture
PROPOSAL: Explore an efficient implementation of the revised ORN using a split-depth architecture, where small and efficient rotation layers are used for early positions, and larger, more complex layers are reserved for deeper positions where more context and positional information is required.
CONTROLS: Compare the trained models with various split-depth settings to the original, fully-agnostic ORN implementation.
COST: 20 GPU-hours (training and evaluating different split-depth architectures)
PREDICTION: This implementation should allow for faster training and evaluation of ORN-based models while maintaining robust performance. However, determining the optimal split-depth setting might require significant experimentation.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Layer-Specific Rotation for Efficient Positional Encoding
PROPOSAL: Introduce a layer-specific rotation (LSR) mechanism, where each transformer layer has its own set of learnable rotation matrices, similar to ORN. This can further boost expressivity and reduce positional encoding overhead by adapting to the local context of each layer.
CONTROLS: Evaluate LSR and ORN on smaller models and select LSR as a stronger competitor to include, and a baseline (simple rotation) for the LSR to beat; since model size can impact outcomes.
COST: 50 GPU-hours (training smaller models with LSR and compare to ORN)
PREDICTION: With LSR, we may see better convergence and low-level contextualization for smaller structures. However, for larger models, LSR could be dominated by ORN in terms of positional encoding ability and stability.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Practical Evaluation of Positional Encoding Formulations on Large Language Models
PROPOSAL: Perform a comprehensive evaluation of the competitive positional encoding formulations (including ORN, LSR, ALiBi, and a strong baseline using learned absolute positions) on a selection of large, publicly available language models (e.g., BERT, RoBERTa, and variants), focusing on real-world downstream tasks and measure their relative performance using metrics like perplexity, accuracy, and ROUGE.
CONTROLS: Run experiments with different language models, task datasets, and positional encoding combinations to evaluate the robustness of the results; compare against a strong absolute position baseline.
COST: 500 GPU-hours (evaluation on large language models)
PREDICTION: This study might reveal that the learned formulations outperform or on-par with absolute position baselines on more tasks, and demonstrate the superior adaptability and contextualization abilities of ORN and LSR. Contrary to expectations, implementation-specific overhead might dwarf the potential benefits for very large models.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Relay Rotation Network for Context-Aware Positional Encoding
PROPOSAL: Explore a novel approach to contextual positional encoding by introducing a relay rotation network (RRN), which uses a hierarchical structure to accumulate and propagate contextual information across different position ranges. Each relay node is associated with a learnable rotation matrix, which refines the contextual representation of the input sequence.
CONTROLS: Compare RRN with standalone ORN, LSR, and ALiBi in achieving contextualization accuracy, using metrics like contextual knowledge transfer and understanding.
COST: 100 GPU-hours (training and evaluating RRN)
PREDICTION: RRN is expected to exhibit strong contextualization capabilities, as it effectively fuses the advantages of hierarchical structures and adaptive rotation matrices. However, it may require careful tuning of the relay structure and rotation matrices to achieve optimal performance.

ACTION: ADD 8
TITLE: Positional Encoding Benchmark Suite for Transformers
PROPOSAL: Develop a comprehensive benchmark suite for evaluating positional encoding formulations on a wide range of transformer architectures and downstream tasks. This benchmark suite will include a diverse set of datasets, tasks, and evaluation metrics, allowing for a comprehensive assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of different positional encoding approaches.
CONTROLS: Use the benchmark suite to analyze the performance of ORN, LSR, ALiBi, and RRN, as well as a strong baseline using absolute positions.
COST: 300 GPU-hours (collecting and evaluating datasets in the benchmark suite)
PREDICTION: The benchmark suite will serve as a valuable resource for the research community, enabling a fair and comprehensive evaluation of different positional encoding formulations and providing insights into their relative strengths and weaknesses.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Formulation for Rotational Positional Encoding
PROPOSAL: Develop a unified theory that generalizes Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) to include additive and forgetting mechanisms, while preserving orthogonality and exact relativity. This is done by adding a bias term that enables scaling of position information, allowing to smoothly transition between rotational and additive/forgetting positional encodings.
CONTROLS: Baseline on RoPE, ALiBi, and FoX on the same experiments, static and adaptive bias ablation to gauge the importance of bias terms.
COST: 1 GPU-hour (theoretical derivation).
PREDICTION: If successful, the unified formulation should allow for generalization across different families of positional encodings, enabling better model expressivity and adaptability. However, the effectiveness of the approach may be limited by its complexity and the added computational cost, potentially leading to overfitting or decreased performance on certain models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Experimental Validation of Unified Formulation
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the proposed unified formulation on a range of real-world language modeling tasks, including transformer-based models fine-tuned on variants of GLUE and SuperGLUE benchmarks. Compare the unified formulation with RoPE, ALiBi, and FoX on tasks that benefit from different types of positional encodings.
CONTROLS: Include RoPE, ALiBi, and FoX as baselines; test both static and adaptive bias configurations of the unified formulation; ablate token types, batch sizes, and near-sequence lengths to isolate effects of positional encoding choices.
COST: 100 GPU-hours (empirical evaluation).
PREDICTION: The unified formulation is expected to significantly outperform other models on tasks where cross-subspace coupling and variable phase warping are beneficial, such as natural language inference and question answering. However, its performance might be similar to RoPE or ALiBi on tasks with fixed context lengths and simple positional structures, leading to a nuanced assessment of its benefits.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Simplified Generative Mechanisms for Positional Encodings
PROPOSAL: Explore reduced-cost rotational positional encoding schemes, where the full matrix exponential is replaced by a simplified generative mechanism. These reduced schemes should aim to approximate the full-matrix exponential or introduce a small explicit error while maintaining orthogonality and ease of adaptability. Examples of such mechanisms include limited-range rotations, circular Fourier transforms, or related Fast Fourier Transform approximations.
CONTROLS: Compare proposed reduced-cost schemes against the original rotational encoding mechanism in terms of accuracy, training computational cost, and inference time.
COST: 50 GPU-hours (parameter tuning and comparison).
PREDICTION: Simplified generative mechanisms could efficiently capture key aspects of Rotary Position Embeddings while allowing for contextual modifications, potentially reducing the overall training computational cost and improving model deployment. However, this simplification might come at the cost of accuracy in certain scenarios, particularly if too much information is sacrificed in the approximation.

This approach enables the model to learn when to use simple approximations and when to rely on more accurate, but computationally expensive, rotations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multidimensional Rotary Position Encoding
PROPOSAL: Extend the idea of Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) to multidimensional spaces by representing each position as a rotation in multiple, coupled subspaces. This can be achieved by introducing orthogonal matrices that project the input sequence onto multiple subspace coordinates, which are then rotated independently. The key challenge lies in developing efficient rotation mechanisms that can adapt to the different subspaces.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of multidimensional rotary position encoding on various tasks, comparing it to the standard 1D RoPE and other positional encoding methods. Investigate different learning strategies for adapting rotations in multiple subspaces, such as shared weights or independent learning for each subspace.
COST: 200 GPU-hours (derivation and empirical evaluation).
PREDICTION: Multidimensional rotary position encoding has the potential to better capture subtle relationships between objects and their positions in complex scenes, leading to improved performance, particularly in tasks that involve scene understanding or spatial-aware language models. However, learning and computing rotations across multiple subspaces can become computationally expensive, potentially limiting the model's scalability and application to real-world tasks.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Unified Formulation for Rotational Positional Encoding
PROPOSAL: Develop a generalized framework that encompasses both multiplicative and additive rotary positional encoding schemes, as well as forgetting mechanisms, by introducing a new parameterized family of orthogonal matrices that admit non-uniform scaling of position information. This allows the model to adapt between the different rotary and additive/forgetting encodings, potentially increasing its expressivity and versatility.
CONTROLS: Keep the ablations of static and adaptive bias configurations of the revised unified formulation. Compare it against RoPE, ALiBi, and FoX on the original tasks from Experimental Validation of Unified Formulation.

PREDICTION: The revised unified formulation provides a more comprehensive and flexible framework for handling positional information in sequence models, potentially opening new avenues for adapting model design to suit specific tasks and datasets. However, the added complexity might lead to overfitting if not properly regularized or controlled. The performance comparison with existing methods should provide insights into the benefits of the unified framework.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Inference-Time Rotational Position Encoding Control
PROPOSAL: Develop a mechanism to dynamically adjust the magnitude or structure of rotational positional encodings during inference, allowing the model to adapt to specific input types or conditioned on contextual information. This could involve introducing conditional rotations or dynamically spawning additional rotations based on input properties, such as sequence length or target identity.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the proposed inferencing-time control on tasks involving adaptive input processing, like sequence-to-sequence models or zero-shot text classification. Compare its performance against fixed rotation schemes and against models without rotational positional encodings.
COST: 150 GPU-hours (model adaptation and empirical evaluation).
PREDICTION: Inference-time rotational position encoding control could potentially unlock adaptive learning capabilities for sequence models, allowing them to adjust their internal representations based on specific deployment scenarios or conditioned contextual information. However, introducing additional control mechanisms may lead to increased model complexity and potential instability under specific conditions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint Learning of Rotational Positional Encodings and Model Parameters
PROPOSAL: Explore algorithms that jointly learn the rotational positional encodings and the model parameters, exploiting the interplay between the two to improve overall performance. This can involve formulating the learning objective as a bilevel optimization problem, where the rotational encoding is optimized as part of the inner loop and the model parameters as part of the outer loop.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of models learned with joint optimization against those with separate optimization of rotational encodings and model parameters. Examine the effect of the learning scheme on the quality of the rotated positional encodings and the resulting model performance.
COST: 250 GPU-hours (joint optimization and empirical evaluation).
PREDICTION: Jointly learning rotational positional encodings and model parameters may lead to enhanced expressivity and adaptability of sequence models, particularly when addressing complex tasks that involve transformation-based positional relationships. However, the added complexity of joint optimization may present challenges, such as requiring more extensive hyperparameter tuning or being more sensitive to initial conditions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Initialization for Rotational Positional Encodings
PROPOSAL: Investigate efficient initialization strategies for the weights and parameters of rotational positional encodings, leveraging techniques such as random projections, orthogonal matrices, or learned initializations that prioritize sparse or interpretable weight distributions. Evaluate these methods for their impact on model convergence, stability, and overall performance across a range of sequence modeling tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed initialization strategies against standard initialization schemes (e.g., glorot-normal, xavier), including experiments with different sequence lengths, batch sizes, and learning rates.
COST: 100 GPU-hours (relatively low-resource initialization studies).
PREDICTION: Developing efficient initialization strategies for rotational positional encodings can have a profound impact on model calibration, convergence speed, and overall performance, particularly in challenging sequence modeling tasks where model capacity is critical. By providing a more informed setup, efficient initialization may also help bridge the gap between theoretical and empirical performance, promoting wider adoption of rotational positional encodings.
